rounds.text: Cosmo First Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, trading at an attractive P/E of 9.7x [E1] compared to a much higher sector benchmark of 21.41x [E6]. This valuation disconnect is further highlighted by an EV/EBITDA of 6.71x against the sector's 12.12x [E11], alongside a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 923 per share surpassing the current price of Rs 826 [E45]. Fundamental momentum is accelerating sharply, evidenced by a 41% surge in trailing twelve-month sales growth [E17] and a 53% leap in trailing profit growth [E21], while operating margins have expanded by 3 percentage points over three years to 10% [E30]. Institutional accumulation is underway with positive money flows showing domestic institutions increasing their stake to 2.18% [E43, E44], backed by a supportive capital goods sector tailwind score of +0.58 [E70, E72] and a rules-based screen score of 76 out of 100 [E64]. Conceded: free cash flow stands at negative Rs 8 Cr for March 2026 [E36], and promoter holdings have decreased by 4.26 percentage points since December 2023 [E41].

The bear case rests on a persistent multi-year deterioration in profitability and shareholder returns, underscored by a compounded profit growth of -7% over 5 years and -13% over 3 years [E19, E20]. This fundamental weakness is mirrored in past share price performance, with compounded returns of -5% over 5 years and -6% over the past year [E23, E25]. Furthermore, insider confidence appears to be waning, as promoter holding has dropped by 4.26 percentage points from December 2023 to September 2026, falling to 40.78% [E41]. Compounded sales growth over the past 5 years has also been low at 10% [E15], accompanied by a negative free cash flow of Rs -8 Cr as of March 2026 [E36]. Compounded further by an inconsistent operating margin trend over the last two years [E32] and a low median return on equity of 8% over the last 3 years [E28], the historical execution leaves substantial room for caution. Conceded: [E21].

Conceded: [E19, E20, E23, E25, E36]. While historical profit and share price metrics show multi-year headwinds, pointing to past weakness ignores the dramatic current inflection where trailing twelve month sales surged 41% and profit skyrocketed 53% [E17, E21]. The bear highlights a drop in promoter holding [E41], but overlooks that institutional money flow is positive with domestic institutions actually increasing their stake by 1.42 percentage points [E43, E44]. Regarding return on equity, while the 3-year median was low [E28], the long-term 10-year and 5-year medians sit much higher at 16% and 15% respectively [E26, E27]. Furthermore, operating margins have expanded to 10% in the TTM period compared to 7% three years earlier [E30], and the business is supported by a capital goods sector tailwind score of +0.58 [E72].

Conceded: [E17, E21, E30, E43, E44, E72]. While trailing twelve-month growth rates and margin expansions appear impressive, they mask a multi-year trend of deteriorating profits, with 5-year and 3-year compounded profit growth resting firmly in negative territory at -7% and -13% respectively [E19, E20]. Pointing to long-term ROE medians [E26, E27] ignores the more recent collapse in capital efficiency, evidenced by a 3-year median ROE of just 8% and official flags noting a low return on equity [E28, E61]. Furthermore, despite the positive shift by domestic institutions [E43], overall promoter holding has persistently declined by 4.26 percentage points over the last three years [E41, E63]. Finally, reliance on sector tailwinds [E72] cannot override company-specific structural drags, such as negative free cash flow of Rs -8 Cr as of March 2026 and an inconsistent operating-margin trend [E32, E36].
